intro: Ask anyone in Amnat Charoen where to stay in town and the name Faikid Hotel comes up near the top of the list · It's a 61-room city hotel on Arunprasert Road in the Bung subdistrict, open since 2015, and a regular pick for both business travellers and tourists · The thing reviews agree on is that the rooms are clean, the beds large and comfortable, and the staff friendly — plus there's the Tiegna restaurant right next door that many guests love to stop at · The location is within walking distance of the Amnat Charoen Clock Tower, Wat Thep Mongkol and the night market, with breakfast included and free parking, from approx. ฿590/night · Real guest reviews call it the most convenient, best-value choice for staying in the centre of town.

body.html: Faikid Hotel — known locally as Rong Raem Fai Khit — is a 61-room city hotel on Arunprasert Road, Samranrat Lane, in the Bung subdistrict of central Amnat Charoen · Open since 2015, it has become one of the first names people think of when visiting the town · The name "Fai Khit" refers to a traditional Isan woven cotton, giving it a local flavour, though the hotel itself is simple and practical rather than design-led or luxurious.

Rooms come in several types, from a Standard Double up to Superior on the 3rd floor, Deluxe and Suite · What guests praise most consistently is that the beds are large and comfortable, the rooms clean, and housekeeping changes the sheets and towels daily · Every room has air conditioning, a refrigerator, a TV and free Wi-Fi, and some have a private balcony · The furnishings are complete and functional — not luxurious, but a good fit for a rate of a few hundred baht · It's exactly the kind of room upcountry travellers want: clean, quiet and easy to sleep in.

"The bed is big and really comfortable, the room is clean and they change the linens every day · there's the Tiegna restaurant right by the hotel for a coffee, the staff are friendly, and at a few hundred baht in the town centre it's good value."

Location is a big reason people choose it · Right in central Amnat Charoen, it's a few minutes' walk to the Amnat Charoen Clock Tower and Wat Thep Mongkol, near the Ming Mongkol junction, the night market, government offices and the hospital · Eateries and convenience stores surround the hotel, so food is easy to find day or night · The on-site Tiegna restaurant gets frequent mentions for its pleasant setting — good for a coffee or dinner — and there's a bamboo bar in the garden for evening drinks, plus free parking, which is very handy for self-drivers.

On breakfast, the hotel serves a Thai-Isan buffet breakfast in the morning, with rice soup, side dishes, fruit and bread · Some Western guests note the Western options are limited and it's mostly Thai food — but for Thai travellers wanting a homely morning meal, it hits the spot · Staff earn praise for being friendly and helpful, though a few reviews mention that English can be a little limited.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: the most frequently mentioned limitation is that there's no lift, and the cheaper rooms are on the upper floors, meaning stairs — something elderly guests or anyone with heavy luggage should plan for · The other is that the in-house karaoke bar can be noisy on some nights, so light sleepers should request a room away from the bar zone · A few reviews mention low water pressure in some bathrooms, and air conditioning that doesn't quite reach the bed in certain rooms · These are small trade-offs for the price and the central location.

In short: if you want a place in central Amnat Charoen with clean rooms, comfy beds, the sights on foot, breakfast and free parking — Faikid Hotel is the most fitting choice in town · The 8.0 from over 421 Agoda reviews, and its #1 ranking among B&Bs/inns in town on TripAdvisor, captures it well · It suits business travellers, those visiting government offices, or anyone stopping over for a night on an Isan trip.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you're a light sleeper or travelling with older relatives, request a ground-floor room away from the karaoke bar at the time of booking · And for the best atmosphere, head to the Tiegna restaurant next to the hotel in the evening for a coffee or dinner — it's the corner guests like most about this place.

honestChecks: If you're travelling with elderly relatives or heavy luggage — there's no lift and the cheaper rooms are upstairs, meaning stairs → request a ground-floor room when you book.
If you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise — the in-house karaoke bar can be loud until late on some nights → request a room away from the bar zone, or avoid Friday-Saturday nights.
If you expect a large hotel with a pool and gym — this is a city hotel focused on clean rooms and location, with no pool → for a pool, look at an out-of-town option like Penpit Hotel.

faq.q: Where is Faikid Hotel in Amnat Charoen, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Faikid Hotel is at 449 Moo 12, Samranrat Lane, Arunprasert Road, Bung subdistrict, in central Amnat Charoen · It's a walk to Wat Thep Mongkol (~0.7 km), the Amnat Charoen Clock Tower and the Ming Mongkol junction (~0.9 km) · It's near the night market, government offices and the hospital · Eateries and convenience stores surround the hotel, so food is easy to find.

faq.q: How much does Faikid Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿590/night for a Standard Double · Superior (3rd floor), Deluxe and Suite rooms run about ฿690–฿1,200 · Prices vary by room type and season, so compare Agoda and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Faikid Hotel have a lift and breakfast?
faq.a: There's a Thai-Isan buffet breakfast, but no lift · The cheaper rooms are upstairs and mean stairs, so request a ground-floor room if you're with elderly relatives or heavy bags · Breakfast leans Thai, with limited Western options.

faq.q: Who is Faikid Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a central Amnat Charoen city hotel with clean rooms, comfy beds and the sights on foot, at a few hundred baht · It suits business travellers, those visiting government offices, or anyone stopping over for a night on an Isan trip · It's less suited to those who need a lift, a pool, or guaranteed total quiet every night.

faq.q: Is Faikid Hotel noisy — is there really a karaoke bar?
faq.a: The hotel has an in-house karaoke bar that can be loud until late on some nights · Light sleepers should request a room away from the bar zone or avoid Friday-Saturday nights · Most reviews say the rooms further away are quiet and easy to sleep in.

faq.q: Is there parking at Faikid Hotel for self-drivers?
faq.a: Yes · The hotel has free on-site parking, ideal if you're driving yourself or stopping over on an Isan route · The Arunprasert Road location is easy to access — central but not on a busy main road.
